title: Constant finite free sheaf morphisms lift locally through epis
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], B a commutative ring, p:F→G an epi of modules over the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], n a natural number, and U an object. Every morphism a:constant(B^n)|U→G|U lifts through p|V after restriction to every member V→U of a covering sieve. Constants and their finite-free comparisons are those of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], and all slice restrictions use [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 093U, lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant (3), constant finite free sheaf morphisms lift locally through epis

proof.text: First replace the source by the finite biproduct of rank-one free sheaves. On the slice over U, a morphism from a rank-one summand is determined by its value at one at the terminal object: naturality propagates that value to all slice objects.
Lift the finitely many values of the summand morphisms through p on a common covering sieve.

On each member V→U the lifted sections define morphisms from the rank-one free sheaves on C/V by the unit-Hom equivalence. Restriction preserves the finite coproduct, so these assemble to a morphism from the restricted biproduct. Naturality and equality on one at the terminal object verify the composite with p.

Use the canonical finite-free comparison to identify constant(B^n) with the product, hence biproduct, of n copies of the ring sheaf. Transport the preceding result through its restricted isomorphism. The finite coproduct and finite-section argument include n=0.

theorem exists_cover_lift_constant_finite_free
    (F G : ringedSiteModules.{u}
      ((constantSheaf J RingCat.{u}).obj (RingCat.of B)))
    (p : F ⟶ G) [Epi p] (n : ℕ) (U : C)
    (a : ((strictPerfectConstantSheaf J B).obj
      (ModuleCat.of B (Fin n → B))).over U ⟶ G.over U) :
    ∃ S ∈ J U, ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
      ∃ l : ((strictPerfectConstantSheaf J B).obj
        (ModuleCat.of B (Fin n → B))).over V ⟶ F.over V,
        l ≫ p.over V =
          (overFunctorMap _ f).inv.app _ ≫ (overMap _ f).map a ≫
            (overFunctorMap _ f).hom.app G
